sources.publisher: Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Company profile — SBIC East Japan
claims: The legal name is Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd.; the company identifies itself as SBIC East Japan.
Corporate number 9011001030621; established 1963-11-15.
Shareholders are described as local governments across 18 prefectures, chambers of commerce, financial institutions and business companies.
The company states it was originally established with some government investment but is now a privatized independent corporation conducting investment activity.
limitations: The profile does not establish any affiliation with SBI Holdings, SBI VC Trade, Ripple, Coinbase or Circle.
Absence of a disclosed relationship is not proof that no commercial contact has ever occurred.

sources.publisher: Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Generative AI (ChatGPT): present and future — SBIC seminar
claims: SBIC Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation hosted a seminar titled Generative AI (ChatGPT): present and future on 2026-03-05.
The seminar program described ChatGPT business-use demonstrations and identified a Microsoft Japan executive evangelist as speaker.
The document lists Hamamatsu Iwata Shinkin Bank as co-host.
limitations: This is an educational event, not evidence of an OpenAI partnership, investment, product integration or XRP relationship.
The speaker's Microsoft affiliation does not make the event a Microsoft-SBIC product partnership.

sources.publisher: Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Generative AI and machine-learning introductory training for manufacturing
claims: The two-day SBIC training program included ChatGPT use on day one and Microsoft Copilot capabilities on day two.
The training was aimed at investee-company personnel and was delivered as an educational program.
limitations: The program does not establish an OpenAI, Microsoft, SBI Holdings or XRP commercial partnership.

sources.publisher: SBI Holdings / SBI VC Trade and Ripple
sources.title: SBI VC Trade begins handling RLUSD in Japan
claims: SBI VC Trade, identified as a consolidated subsidiary of SBI Holdings, announced RLUSD handling on its VCTRADE service beginning 2026-06-24 after maintenance.
SBI VC Trade classified RLUSD under Japan's Type 4 electronic payment instrument framework for its domestic handling; this is the companies' stated Japanese-law classification.
The announcement says deposits and withdrawals are fee-free.
The release describes the listing as a result of the SBI Group and Ripple partnership, with collaboration dating to 2016.
limitations: The Japanese Type 4 classification is reported as the companies' legal characterization; this record is not an independent legal opinion.
The announcement proves distribution availability, not measured RLUSD transaction volume, XRP purchases, XRP collateral deposits or net capital inflows.

sources.publisher: SBI Holdings / SBI VC Trade / Aplus
sources.title: SBI Group and Visa announce a credit card that accrues BTC, ETH and XRP rewards
claims: SBI Holdings announced a Visa-linked credit-card initiative involving SBI VC Trade and Aplus.
The published product description includes BTC, ETH and XRP as reward assets.
limitations: The release establishes a reward-distribution product design, not the amount of XRP purchased, the source of reward inventory, customer uptake or net spot-market demand.

sources.title: RLUSD is now available on Coinbase
claims: RLUSD became available through Coinbase Prime, Coinbase Exchange and the Coinbase retail app.
Deposits and withdrawals are supported on XRPL, Base and Ethereum in supported regions.
Coinbase states Ripple will provide liquidity on Base.
Coinbase Global Exchange collateral use was deferred at launch and described as a future capability.
limitations: Listing and network support do not establish net XRP demand or a measured RLUSD cross-chain flow.
Ripple liquidity support on Base is not a disclosed XRP purchase commitment.

sources.title: XRP ETF flows — 2026-10-30 partial T+1 report
claims: The provider reported +USD 0.2M for 2026-10-30, marked partial with 3 of 5 funds reported.
Reported components were XRPC +USD 0.9M, Bitwise XRP -USD 0.7M and TOXR zero; XRPZ and GXRP were pending.
The provider described its data as T+1 and said the total is recomputed as fund data arrives.
limitations: The report is explicitly partial and cannot be treated as the final five-fund total.
The source is an aggregator, not the ETF issuers' consolidated official report.
Its upstream issuer-file mapping and exact fund-level timestamp alignment were not independently reproduced in this run.

sources.title: XRP ETF flows — 2026-10-30
claims: The provider displayed -USD 496.50K for 2026-10-30 and described all five funds as represented: Bitwise -USD 694K, XRPZ zero, XRPC +USD 922K, GXRP -USD 725K and TOXR zero.
The page says its source is figures reported by the XRP funds each trading day.
limitations: The page does not expose issuer-file publication timestamps or a sufficiently detailed fund-by-fund alignment method in the captured view.
The aggregate is a secondary provider observation and conflicts with other same-date provider displays.

sources.title: XRP ETF flows — issuer-file-derived partial 2026-10-30 observation
claims: The provider displayed -USD 1.412M for 2026-10-30, partial 3 of 4 daily-collected funds: Bitwise -USD 866K, XRPC -USD 545K and TOXR zero; it was waiting for Franklin XRPZ.
It states that flows are changes in XRP holdings from the previous US trading day, converted to USD using its own XRP/USD close.
It excludes Grayscale GXRP from daily totals because its site blocks automated reads; it says it does not work around that restriction.
It describes checking issuer files every five minutes and says the page was updated 2026-10-31 18:03 UTC.
limitations: The source page contains a confusing issuer-file date/timestamp statement for Canary/XRPC; retain the raw page and do not assume all labels map cleanly to the US trading session.
It uses a different daily-collected fund universe from the five-fund CryptoETF/Maketo views.
The USD conversion uses the provider's own XRP/USD close, so USD totals need not match fund-NAV-based values.
